summary: Service account annotation truncation breaks service-account impersonation in private deployment
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that after onboarding to Private deployment, calls that rely on Kubernetes service-account-based impersonation intermittently receive 403s. The failure correlates with long service account annotation values used by the customer's provisioning tooling.

Impact:
- Several backend workers that call Redwood Admin APIs using service-account impersonation receive 403s intermittently (approx 10-20% of requests).
- Affects mission-critical ingestion pipelines and scheduled maintenance jobs.
- Customer is on a Private deployment in us-east and has strict uptime requirements.

Environment:
- Private control plane (customer-managed), prod-us-east region
- Proxy: Envoy edge + internal auth-proxy version 1.14.2
- K8s: EKS 1.25; service accounts annotated via automation (annotations length ~800 characters)

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Customer creates a service account with annotations created by their provisioning tool (annotation value length > 512 bytes).
2) Workload obtains projected service-account token and uses it to call admin endpoints through the private-proxy.
3) ~1 in 5 requests return 403 with authz failure message: "impersonation not permitted: service account mapping mismatch"

Expected behavior:
- Service-account annotation values should be preserved and mapped to the correct tenant/role bindings. Impersonation should succeed when role bindings exist.

Observed behavior:
- Long annotation values appear to be truncated by the ingress/auth-proxy layer. Truncated identity leads to lookup mismatch in RBAC store and a resulting 403. Truncation appears intermittent depending on header chunking and routing path.

Attachments/Logs:
- Customer provided request traces (sampling): trace IDs included in comments below.
- Excerpted proxy debug log attached by customer showing header length and "truncated-annotation" warning.

Notes on urgency:
- Customer marked impact as high due to missed ingestion windows and manual retries. Requested P1 handling and a mitigation path.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 10:45 - Diego Morales (SRE): Confirmed customer traces show annotation header present in original request but truncated at auth-proxy. Observed header size approaching 1024 bytes on some requests.

2026-03-10 13:20 - Diego Morales (SRE): Hypothesis: Envoy header size limit or internal buffer in auth-proxy cuts long annotation values. Need to check envoy_max_request_headers_kb and proxy header handling (we set a default 8KB at platform but private control plane proxies may override).

2026-03-11 09:02 - Lina Chen (Platform Eng): Reproduced locally with a synthetic request using a service account annotation of 900 bytes. Auth-proxy (1.14.2) drops last 384 bytes intermittently when HTTP/2 frames split differently. Reproducible when multiplexing enabled.

2026-03-11 11:55 - Diego Morales (SRE): Cross-referenced with linked ticket SUP-30121 (proxy-jwks-cache-stale-admin-console-403s) for similar proxy header truncation patterns. Considered whether TLS record sizing affects fragmentation.
2026-03-12 08:10 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer confirmed they upgraded provisioning tool recently which increased encoded annotation length (added extra metadata and tenant labels).
comments: 2026-03-10 11:05 - Customer (FinAnalyze) - initial: We're seeing intermittent 403s after moving to private. We dug into logs and see the annotation looks truncated in some request headers. Attaching a sample request and the k8s SA manifest.
2026-03-10 12:30 - Aisha Patel (Support): Thanks for the details — we will triage this and pull in SRE/Platform. Can you confirm the typical annotation length and whether you use HTTP/2 at the edge?
2026-03-10 13:10 - Customer (FinAnalyze): Annotation lengths vary; some are ~800-900 chars. Edge uses HTTP/2 and an external ALB in front of our proxies.

2026-03-11 10:00 - Diego Morales (SRE): Reproduced locally. Tentative finding: auth-proxy v1.14.2 has an edge case where very long headers combined with HTTP/2 framing cause trailing bytes to be dropped when header compression/context is reused. Working on a minimal repro and patch.

2026-03-11 15:45 - Lina Chen (Platform Eng): Temporary mitigation: recommend trimming annotation values to <400 characters or move less-essential metadata to a config map for now. We'll prepare a hotfix for auth-proxy to handle larger headers reliably.
2026-03-12 09:30 - Customer (FinAnalyze): We can trim annotations as a stopgap but need a platform fix. Please advise ETA for hotfix and any rollout caveats for private control plane.

2026-03-12 10:05 - Diego Morales (SRE): ETA for hotfix patch release to auth-proxy: 2026-03-16 (staged rollout). For private control plane customers we will provide a patch image and rollout instructions; patch is non-breaking but requires a rolling restart of proxy pods.
2026-03-12 10:20 - Aisha Patel (Support): Noted. Logged follow-up action to schedule phone bridge with customer for patch window and to verify trimmed-annotation mitigation.
2026-03-12 13:40 - Customer (FinAnalyze): Confirmed trimmed-annotation mitigates failures for our ingestion jobs. Waiting on patch for full resolution.
resolution: Workaround applied: customer trimmed service-account annotations to <400 characters to avoid truncation. Engineering identified header handling bug in auth-proxy v1.14.2 that can drop trailing bytes for very long headers when HTTP/2 framing splits compressed header blocks. Next steps: create and release auth-proxy hotfix (target 2026-03-16), publish private control plane rollout instructions, and add a KB article recommending annotation length limits and how to move metadata to configmaps. Post-release: verify customer production traces and close ticket.
next_steps: Publish hotfix for auth-proxy and provide image tag to private customers
Work with customer to schedule rolling restart during maintenance window
Add annotation-length recommendation to onboarding docs and KB
Follow up in 72h after patch rollout to confirm absence of 403s
